children: The number of Australian job advertisements rose for a fifth straight month in September, private-sector data showed on Monday, suggesting labour demand remained healthy despite higher borrowing costs.
The number of job advertisements rose 2.2% in September from August, when they gained 2.6%, according to data from Australia and New Zealand Banking Group
and employment website Indeed. Ads were up 12.9% from a year earlier and 24.4% above their decade-long average.
Australia's jobless rate edged up to a five-year high of 4.6% in August even as employment rose, with more people looking for work.
